title: John 8:31–47
context: Jesus turns to Jews who had believed him, If you remain in my word, then you are truly disciples; you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free. They protest Abrahamic freedom. He answers that everyone who commits sin is the bondservant of sin; a bondservant doesn’t live in the house forever, but a son does; if therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed. Offspring of Abraham still seek to kill him because his word finds no place in them. Abraham’s children would do Abraham’s works; instead they do their father’s. They claim God as Father; he says if God were their Father they would love him. They cannot bear to hear his word because they are of their father the devil, a murderer and liar. Whoever is of God hears God’s words; the reason they do not hear is that they are not of God.

verses.text: Jesus therefore said to those Jews who had believed him, “If you remain in my word, then you are truly my disciples.
verses.arminianNotes:
The if is aimed at people John has just called believers. Abiding in his word is the mark of being truly disciples—not a one-time nod in the treasury. Remaining is how faith proves it is not a mood.

Classical Arminians take the condition at full strength. Beginning well is not finishing. Prevenient and cooperating grace make abiding possible; it can still be refused. True discipleship is continuance in the word, not a label that cannot be lost by walking away from that word.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: it is not enough to have begun well if progress to the end does not correspond. He exhorts to perseverance those who have tasted his doctrine. Many profess discipleship who are not so in reality; hypocrites give way at the start or in the middle, believers persevere to the end.

The if sorts true disciples from temporary believers. Abiding is the Spirit’s fruit in those actually given to the Son, not a hoop a regenerate person may finally fail. The address is still a serious exhortation to this crowd.
verses.keyContrast: Both refuse a faith that never continues. Arminians find a condition: abiding is required, grace-enabled, and resistible—discipleship can fail by not remaining. Reformed readers commonly hear the same if as the way true disciples are distinguished from hypocrites: those who belong will persevere, and continuance is the evidence, not an uncertain lottery.

verses.text: You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.”
verses.arminianNotes:
Promise chained to abiding: know the truth, and that truth frees. Wesley: the truth written in the heart by the Spirit frees from guilt, sin, misery, Satan. Freedom is not pedigree; it is a gift that arrives in the word remaining in you.

Arminians preach this as an offer of liberty. The Son means to free these hearers. Remaining in the word is how one comes into that knowledge; refusing the word is how one stays bound while quoting Abraham.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: those who have some knowledge shall know the truth—progress by gift on gift. He impresses the word on hearts by his Spirit and chases ignorance. The fruit is freedom from Satan, sin, and death. By nature we are slaves; regeneration makes us free to obey righteousness; freedom has degrees according to faith’s measure.

The truth that frees is not a slogan. It is Christ in the Gospel, restoring liberty none of us hold by bloodline. Papist free-will boasts are exactly what this verse unmasks.

verses.text: They answered him, “We are Abraham’s offspring, and have never been in bondage to anyone. How do you say, ‘You will be made free’?”
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: the other Jews standing by, not those who believed, as the conversation’s tenor shows. “Never enslaved” is a notorious untruth; they were under Rome. Ancestry is their gospel; freedom offered as future gift feels like insult.

Pride can answer for a whole crowd. The offer of freedom is still on the table. They would rather defend a false liberty than confess a yoke. That is how grace is refused in public.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: perhaps a mixed crowd, as Scripture often ascribes to all what belongs to a part. They cannot endure that a holy elect people should be called slaves. They had this excuse—that unjust occupation did not cancel covenant right—yet they missed that Abraham’s freedom stands only in the Mediator, and that degenerate sons are not lawful children without the Spirit’s regeneration.

False confidence in the flesh drives away the grace of Christ. Almost no one feels he needs that grace while he can still say “Abraham.”

verses.text: Jesus answered them, “Most certainly I tell you, everyone who commits sin is the bondservant of sin.
verses.arminianNotes:
Truly, truly: practice of sin is slavery, not a hobby. Wesley: he that commits sin is in fact the slave of sin. The bondage is moral and spiritual before it is political. They asked about becoming free; he names the chain they will not see.

Classical Arminians agree this slavery is true—no Pelagian shrug. They still hold that the slave is addressed with a genuine “If therefore the Son makes you free.” Inability to self-liberate does not undo the sincere offer of the Son’s freeing work.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: deeper than the philosophers’ “lust makes slaves.” Christ describes the condition of nature, not only bad choices: all not delivered by him are in slavery; all who derive sin’s contagion from corrupted nature are slaves from birth. Yet the slavery is voluntary—they who necessarily sin are not compelled as if dragged against their will.

Necessity and willingness stand together. No one frees himself; the diagnosis is why the Son must do the freeing, not why the command to come is a feint.
verses.keyContrast: Both confess bondage to sin, not mere bad examples. Arminians typically keep the slave genuinely addressable by the Son’s freeing word, grace restoring the ability to yield. Reformed commentators read practicing-sin slavery as native corruption from birth, voluntary yet needing the Son’s deliverance that actually creates freedom.

verses.text: A bondservant doesn’t live in the house forever. A son remains forever.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: all sinners shall be cast out of God’s house as the slave was out of Abraham’s; the Son abides forever. Remaining in the house is sonship, not a temporary live-in. The warning is to people who think Abraham’s address is a permanent lease.

Does not remain is an eviction. Privilege without the Son’s freedom expires. The same house still has a Son who would have them stay as freed children, not as squatters on a name.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: from household law—a slave may have power for a time yet is not the heir. No perfect, durable freedom except through the Son. They hold a mask: place in the church like Ishmael rising against the freeborn for a short time.

Empty title is not inheritance. Those who merely occupy Abraham’s house without the Son will not remain. The son’s forever is Christ’s, then theirs by adoption into him.

verses.text: If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.
verses.arminianNotes:
The if again, now with the Son as Liberator. Wesley: if I make you free, you partake of the same privilege; freed from all guilt and sin, you shall abide in God’s house forever. Indeed-freedom is offered, not a metaphor. He means this crowd could be free.

Arminians preach this as liberty: the Son sets sinners free, and the condition is receiving that work, abiding in his word. This is not autonomy; it is freedom from sin’s slavery into the house. A freedom that cannot be refused is not the freedom this verse puts in an if.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: the right of freedom belongs to the Son alone; all others, born slaves, cannot be delivered but by his grace. What he has by nature he imparts by adoption when we are ingrafted by faith into his body. The Gospel is the instrument; he regenerates by his Spirit. Truly free stands against their foolish persuasion that they already possess a kingdom while in wretched bondage.

Free indeed is the Son’s work, not self-emancipation. The if is the way of faith-union, not a maybe at the throne. Those he frees are not almost-free.
verses.keyContrast: No dispute here: only the Son gives freedom worthy of the name. Arminians detect a sincere, conditional offer of liberty to these enslaved hearers. Calvinists hear that none but the Son can free, and that those born slaves are actually delivered only when he ingrafts them—true freedom, not a title.

verses.text: I know that you are Abraham’s offspring, yet you seek to kill me, because my word finds no place in you.
verses.arminianNotes:
He grants flesh-descent and denies spiritual kinship. Wesley: Abraham’s offspring after the flesh, not followers of Abraham’s faith; the word has no place in their hearts. Murder-intent is the evidence. Space for the word is the issue, not missing ancestry.

“No place” is a refusal of room. The word is present enough to kill over. They could have given it place; they seek instead to silence the Speaker. That is responsible unbelief, not a quietly absent decree doing all the work.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: concession that ridicules their title. What avails being called Abraham’s children if they rage against God and his ministers and rush to shed innocent blood? They cannot receive his words because through malice they keep their minds shut.

Malice shutting the mind is itself the mark of a nature not yet opened. The word finds no place because the house is already occupied by another father, as the next verses will say.

verses.text: I say the things which I have seen with my Father; and you also do the things which you have seen with your father.”
verses.arminianNotes:
Two fathers teach two curricula. He speaks from sight with the Father; they act from what they have heard from theirs—not yet named. Deeds already disclose the household.

The contrast is meant to wake them. They are doing a father’s will they have chosen to hear. The unnamed father is still a warning, not a tattoo they cannot repent of if they would receive the Son’s word.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: argument from contraries—he brings only what he learned from his Father; their fury at God’s word shows an opposite father. He speaks (office of teacher); they do (labor to extinguish the doctrine).

Opposition to the Gospel is not surprising in children of the devil. The next lines will strip the remaining masks of Abraham and of God-as-Father.

verses.text: They answered him, “Our father is Abraham.” Jesus said to them, “If you were Abraham’s children, you would do the works of Abraham.
verses.arminianNotes:
They repeat the title; he adds an if of resemblance. Abraham’s children do Abraham’s works—faith that receives God’s word, not a plot to kill the speaker of truth. Lineage without likeness is a lie they tell themselves.

“If you were… you would be doing.” Works do not buy sonship; they show it. The door of becoming true children by faith, as Abraham believed, is the same door Paul will preach—and it is still in front of them.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: he distinguishes bastards from lawful children and will not give the name to those who do not resemble Abraham. Carnal descent without faith is a false pretense. They who reject the promised blessing exclude themselves from Abraham’s family; children of the promise must be born of the Spirit.

Reformed election-note here is not generic: election dwells in Abraham’s seed, yet is free, so that those God sanctifies by the Spirit are the heirs. Empty covering produces hardened opposition to Christ.

verses.text: But now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham didn’t do this.
verses.arminianNotes:
Abraham welcomed messengers from God; they hunt this man for telling truth he heard from God. The contrast is concrete. Murder of a truth-teller is not Abraham’s family custom.

They are not doomed by DNA. They are contradicting Abraham in time. The truth is still being told; they may yet do what Abraham did—believe God.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: the effect proves they are not God’s children as they boasted. Nothing in Abraham is more commended than obedience of faith. Empty titles mean nothing with God. Hatred of true doctrine marks the other family.

Seeking to kill the truth-speaker is the work that names the father. This is not what Abraham did—full stop. Resemblance, not slogan, is the test.

verses.text: You do the works of your father.” They said to him, “We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father, God.”
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: he still does not name the father; when they claim God, then the devil will be named (v. 44). They hear a slur on birth—perhaps even a jab at Jesus’ own origin—and climb to the highest title: God is our Father.

Religious people can answer a moral charge with a higher slogan. “God” is not a saving confession when it is used to dodge the works. Fatherhood will be tested by love of the sent Son.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: they imagine God bound to Abraham’s whole seed: adopted family, therefore we are God’s children. They think they have holiness from the womb. Hypocrites separate God from his word, the church from faith, heaven from the Spirit.

The same boast lives wherever succession or parentage is treated as a claim-check on God. Christ will not grant the title to those who have corrupted the seed of life.

verses.text: Therefore Jesus said to them, “If God were your father, you would love me, for I came out and have come from God. For I haven’t come of myself, but he sent me.
verses.arminianNotes:
Another if: God’s children love the sent Son. Wesley: I proceeded forth as God, and come as Christ. Love of Jesus is not extra credit; it is the family resemblance. Coming from God and being here is the reason love is obligatory.

The if is an unmasking and an earnest invitation. They ought to love him; they may still. Hatred of the sent One is how one shows God is not Father, not how one discovers a hidden non-election and shrugs.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: whoever is a child of God will acknowledge his first-born Son; you hate me, therefore you have no reason to boast that you are God’s children. No piety where Christ is rejected. He speaks of office more than essence: nothing in him is contrary to God.

Love of the Son is not a later hobby of the devout. It is the evidence of having God as Father. Those formed by the Spirit love the One the Father sent.

verses.text: Why don’t you understand my speech? Because you can’t hear my word.
verses.arminianNotes:
Cannot is explained, not left as a brute fact. Wesley: ye cannot—such is your stubbornness and pride—hear, that is, receive, obey. Not being desirous to do his will, they cannot understand (7:17). The inability is moral: they will not bear the word.

Classical Arminians take cannot seriously as present incapacity of a proud heart, and still as culpable. Grace has been shining in the temple; stubbornness is how they cannot. A cannot caused by pride is not an excuse; it is the charge.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: he reproaches obstinacy so great they cannot endure to hear him, and infers diabolical rage. Why-question takes out of their hands the boast that reason and judgment lead them to oppose him. Stupidity in the first clause; ungovernable hatred in the second.

Cannot bear the word is more than a bad mood. It is the slave-nature and the other father showing. That does not make them victims of a capricious ban; it makes their opposition the sign of whose they are.
verses.keyContrast: Both hear a cannot. Arminians typically trace it to stubbornness and pride that will not receive—an inability that remains responsible and that grace still confronts. Reformed Christians take the cannot as the deep inability of those not of God, whose hatred of the word discloses a nature that will not hear unless made otherwise.

verses.text: You are of your father the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and doesn’t stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks on his own; for he is a liar, and the father of lies.
verses.arminianNotes:
The unnamed father is named. Will is to do his desires: murder and lie are the family trade. Wesley: murderer in inclination from the beginning of his becoming a devil; he did not abide in the truth; killer of men from the world’s start. When he speaks a lie, he speaks of his own—origin of lies and of evil in general.

This is not a taunt at ethnicity. It is a moral paternity they are enacting by seeking to kill a truth-teller. “You want” keeps agency on the table. They are not puppets; they like their father’s work. The Son still tells the truth in their hearing.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: children of the devil not only by imitation but by his instigation—he blinds, moves to unrighteousness, exercises tyranny. Not a Manichean second creator: it is corruption of nature whose cause is revolt, not a substance God made evil. Satan was not wicked by creation; he did not remain in the truth.

Their will matches the devil’s desires. That is why truth is intolerable. The verse describes fallen agency under a tyrant, not an innocent nature trapped by a mean God.

verses.text: But because I tell the truth, you don’t believe me.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: because I speak the truth—which liars hate. The causal is devastating: truth is the reason for unbelief, not a lack of evidence. They would believe a fellow liar more readily.

This is chosen allergy to truth. The same truth is still the instrument of freedom (v. 32). Not-believing because it is true is the height of responsible darkness.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: he confirms the preceding—they have no other reason for opposing but that truth is hateful and intolerable, and so they show they are children of Satan.

Unbelief here is not a waiting period for more light. It is hatred of light because it is light. That is why “of God” and “not of God” will be the next criterion.

verses.text: Which of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me?
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: is not my life as unreprovable as my doctrine? Behavior confirms the teaching. No conviction of sin in him leaves them without a moral alibi for unbelief.

The why is a question they ought to answer. If they cannot convict him, the honest path is to believe. Remaining in unbelief after a sinless speaker of truth is inexcusable.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: the question proceeds from perfect confidence. He does not claim they have not slandered him; he means no crime dwells in him. The defense is of his ministry more than a treatise on the Son’s unique impeccability in the abstract: why, if I speak truth, do you not believe?

They have no charge, only a father who cannot stand the truth. The unanswered why is itself evidence of the next verse.

verses.text: He who is of God hears the words of God. For this cause you don’t hear, because you are not of God.”
verses.arminianNotes:
Whoever is of God hears. Wesley: he that is of God—that either loves or fears him—hears with joy and reverence the words God preaches through Christ. Not-hearing is traced to not being of God in the sense of not loving or fearing him—not a shrug that they never had a chance.

Arminians will not erase “you are not of God.” They read it as present spiritual location: not in God’s family by faith and love. The words are still being spoken; hearing remains the duty and the gift of those who will love the Father in the Son. Conditionality of abiding (v. 31) and this verdict belong together: remaining in unbelief is how one shows one is not of God.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: he takes for granted that he is the Father’s faithful ambassador, then kindles: they have nothing in common with God, for they do not hear God’s words. Without talking about himself, he charges them with being at war with God. There is not a more evident sign of a reprobate mind than when one cannot endure Christ’s doctrine; cheerfully embracing it is a visible seal of election.

8:47 is not generic talk of election imported from elsewhere. Jesus himself says they do not hear because they are not of God. True children hear; those not of God cannot. That is why “If you remain” revealed true disciples, and why you cannot bear to hear had a father underneath it.
verses.keyContrast: Fair reading, no straw men. Arminians typically take “of God” as the family of those who love and fear him, so not-hearing is culpable unbelief and proud unwillingness—abiding still sincerely offered. Reformed commentators take Jesus at v. 47 as stating the deep reason: they do not hear because they are not of God—true children versus those whose inability to hear discloses they are not his.
